mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production and economic activity, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% indicates a broad-based fall in demand for goods and housing, which reduces corporate revenues and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating change in PAYEMS (i.e., month-over-month change in PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months) signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month change increases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly increases in RSAFS and subsequent S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as rising household savings can signal increased precautionary behavior but also future consumption rebound, boosting near-term market optimism.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly RSAFS increases and positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns falls below 0.3 or is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.
